sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 86

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 86:1
items.html: At the time of the coupling of Gadlut, when through the illumination of the upper AB-SAG the Yud descends from the air of Mocha deAvira, and light remains — then the hairs depart from upon the forehead and the face, and the forehead is revealed, as in Answer 22 above, see there. This is called 'the time of will,' for then the forehead of will is revealed, as written there. (Page 368, Items 156-157).
